_readme: The goddess who brought you over (js/logic/goddess.js, docs/GODDESS.md). Numbers are in balance.json -> goddess.
All player-facing prose is written in second person (you/your); {sam} is used only when Seliora speaks your name aloud.
Placeholders: {goddess} her name, {sam}, {house}, {partner} (first name), {past} (your past life, lowercase), {lady} (a lady's first name), {n}, {names}, {cycle}, {skill}.
Any text field may be a list: one entry is picked at random.

rebirth: at every New Game+ before the binding. fast/steady/slow = how quickly you paid (weeks vs the plan). lovers/alone = lovers carried or none. jealous.low/mid/high by her jealousy. bound.low/mid/high = after the binding, by her divinity.

teases: her scenes before the binding, picked by evGoddess: story scenes (non-repeat) play in file order, each once, from minCycle on; maxCycle is only when they're due, a missed one stays available and makes her visit more often. Repeat scenes are filler, gated by minCycle-maxCycle, and only show once every unlocked story scene has been seen.

distract: what happens when a disguise tease turns into her 'distracting' you (goddess.js evGoddessDistract). lead[phase] (stranger/suspicion/reveal/game) leads in; acts[service] is what she does without letting you finish; dry[tier] is how she leaves you (1 = kisses: just wanting more; 2-3 = high and dry); button[tier] is the button before the ending.

intro.title: A Lantern in the Dark
intro.text:
The streetlamp outside your office window flickers once—not the orange sputter of cheap whale oil, but a steady, warm gold that doesn't belong to any wick in Hollowmere.

When you turn around, she is already perched on the corner of your desk, swinging one bare heel in the air. She looks like a woman in her mid-twenties with night-black hair pinned with a brass crescent, warm amber eyes that catch the lamplight like coins, and a dark travelling cloak draped loosely over clothes that belong to no guild in town.

"You're handling the books surprisingly well, {sam}," she says, tilting her head with a small, amused smile. "I brought you across because I needed someone stubborn enough to keep a lantern lit in a dark corner of the world. I didn't expect you to actually balance the ledger."

She slides off the desk, close enough that you smell ozone, warm wax, and night air. "Keep going. Build something worth keeping. I'll be watching—and don't bother looking for me in the crowd. You won't spot me until I want you to."
intro.res:
She pauses at the window, one hand on the sill, and looks back over her shoulder with that infuriatingly knowing grin.

"Someone who owes you a favor, and intends to collect a few more first. Mind the debt, {sam}."

binding.title: The Lantern's Tether
binding.offer:
She doesn't appear at the window tonight. She is already standing beside your bed when you close the door—no disguise, no borrowed cloak, just night-black hair threaded with gold and eyes burning like banked coals.

"You've done enough," Seliora says softly, and for once there is no teasing in her voice. "You built a house that holds, you kept your word when it would have been easier to fold, and you didn't look away when I showed you what I am."

She steps close enough that the warmth of her skin radiates through your shirt, taking your hands and pressing them flat against her waist. "A god can't walk Hollowmere whole without an anchor in mortal flesh. If you take me tonight—all the way, without holding back—the tether binds. I stay here, with you, in a body that can bleed and tire and belong to someone."

Her fingers tighten around your wrists. "Say yes, {sam}, and there's no undoing it."

binding.noRes:
Seliora blinks, then lets out a long, shaky breath that turns into a quiet laugh. She presses her forehead briefly against your collarbone.

"Still careful with me," she murmurs. "All right. I won't go far—ask when you're ready."

You find her perched on the edge of your bed, bare legs swinging, amber eyes bright in the candlelight. "You've been keeping me waiting, {sam}. Come here."

The room is warm with cedar smoke and her skin is already flushed when she pulls you down onto the quilts, hands already working at your belt.

ending.title: The Lantern Held
ending.text:
The golden spark inside Seliora has finally woven itself into the bones of Hollowmere—no longer a fading tether, but a steady flame that belongs entirely to this world and to the house you built.

She stands beside you on the balcony overlooking the lantern-lit street, resting her chin lightly on your shoulder. "The debt is paid, the lamps are lit, and I'm still here," she says softly. "What do you want to build next, {sam}?"
ending.stayRes: Seliora threads her fingers through yours and leans into your side, smiling as the streetlamps flare warm gold down the avenue.
ending.releaseRes: She kisses your forehead—a warm, lingering touch that smells of cedar and starlight—and steps back into the golden dusk, leaving a single brass lantern burning on your desk.

neglect: You haven't visited Seliora's room in weeks; when you pass her in the corridor, she gives you a cool, measured smile that doesn't quite reach her eyes.
Seliora leans in your doorway with arms crossed, amber eyes narrowed. "I didn't bind myself to mortal clay just to watch you marry your ledger, {sam}."

low: "You're pacing again," Seliora observes from the windowsill, swinging one ankle. "The numbers won't change just because you glare at them."
"Have you eaten today, {sam}, or are you subsisting entirely on tea and stubbornness?"
"Your staff talks about you when you leave the room, you know. Mostly nicely. Which is frankly alarming."
mid: "You've been spending a great deal of time upstairs lately, {sam}," Seliora remarks lightly, though her amber eyes are sharp. "Don't forget who keeps your lanterns lit."
"Another late night with the staff?" She leans against your doorframe with a slow, unreadable smile. "I'm beginning to feel neglected."
high: "I brought you into this world, {sam}, and lately I barely get a nod in the corridor," Seliora says softly, her eyes glowing like banked coals. "Careful."
"Keep ignoring me for the rest of the house, and see what happens to your quiet evenings."

teases.title: Behind the Dyers' Lane

image.comp: a striking dark-haired woman in a velvet travelling cloak pinning him against a brick alley wall, playful half-lidded smile
image.setting: narrow cobblestone alley at dusk, warm lantern glow

teases.intro:
The market has been a long, loud errand: lamp oil, fresh linen, and a haggle over soap that you lost on principle. You're cutting through the narrow lane behind the dyers' street, arms full of parcels, when the evening light goes strangely warm.

A hand closes on your wrist—a very warm hand, with firm, unhurried fingers. Before you have time to protest, your parcels are stacked neatly on the cobbles, your back is against the cool brick of the alley wall, and {form} is smiling up at you from inches away.

"Hold still and I'll show you," {alias} says, tilting her chin up until all you can see are her amber eyes.
teases.wonder:
You have never seen this woman in your life. She smells faintly of cedar smoke, wax, and night air, and she is standing entirely too close for a stranger in a back alley.

Your sensible brain tells you to step aside and pick up your soap. The rest of you hasn't moved an inch.
teases.text: You're cutting through the narrow lane behind the dyers' street with your arms full of parcels when {form} catches your wrist, sets your bundles neatly on the cobbles, and backs you against the cool brick wall. "Hold still and I'll show you," {alias} murmurs, tilting her face up to yours.

choices.label: Let her kiss you
choices.res: She rises onto her toes and kisses you slowly, tasting of spiced wine and warm night air. By the time a cart rattles past the mouth of the lane and she slips away into the dusk, you're leaning against the brick wondering what just happened.
choices.resIn: You don't pull back. You let your hands settle at her waist, and {alias} hums softly against your mouth before drawing you deeper into the shadow of the archway.

choices.label: "Do I know you?"
choices.res: "Not yet," {alias} says, brushing her thumb across your cheekbone with an amused little smile. "Mind your parcels, {sam}." She steps around the corner—and when you look a second later, the lane is completely empty.

teases.title: Three Minutes of Quiet

image.comp: a poised woman in an embroidered crimson jacket leaning against a closed storeroom door, arms behind her back, amused gaze
image.setting: linen storeroom, shelves of folded sheets, warm high window light

teases.intro:
The linen storeroom is the one place in {house} that is always quiet, which is why you go there when you need to think. Today you need fresh towels, and three minutes where nobody asks you a question.

You have an armful of folded sheets when the door clicks shut behind you. You turn around. {form} is leaning against the latch with her hands behind her back, bathed in dusty gold light from the high window, looking you over the way a buyer looks over a display she has already decided to take home.

"You work too hard," {alias} says, as if the two of you had been talking all morning. "Put those down."
teases.wonder: You put them down. You have no idea why; your hands just obey. Maybe because no one in Hollowmere has ever looked at you quite like that—like you're the most interesting thing in the room, and she has all afternoon to prove it.
teases.text: You slip into the linen storeroom for three minutes of peace, only for the door to click shut behind you. {form} leans against the wood with her hands behind her back, looking you over with warm, amused amber eyes. "You work too hard," {alias} says. "Put those down."

choices.label: Step closer
choices.res: She meets you halfway between the shelves, warm and unhurried, leaving you flushed and breathless when a knock finally sounds outside the door. When you glance back, the room is empty and the latch is open a crack.
choices.resIn: You set the towels on the shelf and close the distance between you. {alias} smiles like a cat with the cream, her fingers curling straight into the front of your shirt.

choices.label: "This is a staff-only room."
choices.res: "Is it?" {alias} glances around at the folded sheets with theatrical solemnity. "My mistake. Don't work yourself into the ground, {sam}." She slips out into the hall before you can ask how she knew your name.

teases.title: Cold Tea

image.comp: a slender woman in round spectacles and a scholar's coat seated across a small table, chin in her hand, warm knowing smile
image.setting: quiet corner of a tavern lounge in afternoon light, two teacups

teases.intro:
It is a slow afternoon, and you have sat down at the corner table to let your tea go cold while you tally the week's laundry bills.

When you look up from the column of numbers, {form} is already sitting across from you, chin resting in her palm, watching you over the rim of a second cup you definitely didn't pour.

"You furrow your brow when you add," {alias} remarks mildly, adjusting her round spectacles. "It's endearing, in a tragic sort of way."
teases.wonder: Every instinct says you should ask who let her in before opening hours. Instead, you realize you're enjoying the company—and that her foot has just nudged your ankle under the table.
teases.text: You sit down in the empty lounge to let your tea go cold over the accounts, only to find {form} seated across from you with her chin in her palm. "You furrow your brow when you add," {alias} remarks mildly.

choices.label: Say nothing and hold her gaze
choices.res: You finish the tea eventually, and realize it is the only warm thing left at the table besides your face. You don't mention to anyone why your collar is crooked for the rest of the afternoon.
choices.resIn: You say nothing, and {alias} hums approvingly, her hand sliding smoothly across your knee under the table with complete, unhurried confidence.

choices.label: "Are you looking for a room?"
choices.res: "Only the view," {alias} replies, standing up and smoothing her coat. "Keep at it, {sam}. You're doing better than you think."

teases.title: Evening Rush

image.comp: a lithe dark-haired woman in crimson and gold silks leaning close beside him at a crowded bar counter, teasing smile
image.setting: crowded lantern-lit lounge at night, warm amber glow

teases.intro:
The evening rush is in full cry—glasses clinking, laughter rising from the booths, and a lute playing somewhere near the hearth—and you are wedged against the end of the bar checking tabs.

A warm hip bumps yours, completely unhurried, and {form} is simply there beside you, smelling of jasmine and candle wax. She leans in close enough that her shoulder brushes your chest.

"Ask," says {alias}, with a smile like a dare. "I'm listening."
teases.wonder: The lounge is packed, half your staff is watching from the stairs, and she looks entirely ready to make a scene if you hesitate.
teases.text: During the height of the evening rush, {form} wedges herself beside you at the bar, hip pressed warm against yours. "Ask," says {alias}, with a smile like a dare. "I'm listening."

choices.label: Play along
choices.res: The crowd shifts, someone shouts for a refill, and when you look back she is gone. You spend the rest of the shift touching your collar and trying to look composed.
choices.resIn: You pocket your embarrassment and lean into her. {alias} smiles against your jaw, and the noise of the room seems to retreat a step.

choices.label: "Tell me your real name."
choices.res: "Pay attention, and you won't need to ask," {alias} murmurs, tapping the tip of your nose before melting back into the crowd.

teases.title: Always the Same

image.comp: a woman in a dark travelling cloak leaning over a man's shoulder at a candlelit desk, reading a slip of paper with a delighted smirk
image.setting: small office at night, warm candle on the desk

teases.intro:
You have made a list. It's a short, embarrassing list, written on the back of an invoice with a pencil you keep sharpening: a fox, a cat, an elf, a dwarf. Four columns: hair, eyes, skin, smell. Every line says the same thing four times.

You're still staring at it when the door opens without a knock. {alias} walks in as if she lived here, {form}, and drifts around the desk. She reads the list over your shoulder, and you feel her chin settle on it, smoke and warmth against your neck.

"What's this?" she asks lightly. "Homework?"
teases.wonder:
"A coincidence," you say, and she laughs, a low, delighted sound. It is the same laugh. Of course it is. You just never noticed, because the ears were different.

Your pencil is still in your hand, and her fingers are sliding around your waist.
teases.text: You're staring at an embarrassing list of strangers—fox, cat, elf, dwarf, all with the exact same hair, eyes, and scent—when {alias} drifts behind your desk, {form}, and reads it over your shoulder. "What's this?" she asks lightly.

choices.label: "You know exactly why."
choices.res: "Do I?" Her breath on your neck is hot enough to hurt. "Maybe I'm just a bad girl. Maybe you're just unlucky." She nips your ear, and the door closes behind nobody.
choices.resIn: You feel her go quiet, very briefly, against your spine. Then her hands move again, as though it were all part of the plan.

choices.label: "Stay. Please."
choices.res: "Oh, I'd love to." She does—right up until you're about to tip over the edge. Then you're alone with your list and a racing pulse.
choices.resIn: She goes very soft at that. "Oh, I'd love to," she says, and turns your chair around so she can look at you properly.

teases.title: Smoke and Candle

image.comp: a striking woman in a dark cloak standing by a candlelit desk, amber eyes glowing warmly, holding his tie
image.setting: dim study at night, dozens of warm candle flames

teases.intro:
You can't stop thinking about the dream—gold lanterns swinging in the dark, hundreds of them, and a woman laughing from somewhere just out of sight. Every time you reach for the details in daylight, they slide away like water.

Then {alias} slips through your office door, {form}, and the scent of cedar smoke and warm candle wax hits you all at once. Your hand freezes over the ledger.

She sees the exact moment the pieces click behind your eyes, and her smile turns slow and dangerous. "Oh, you're going to pay for that look," she promises, stepping forward to take hold of your collar.
teases.wonder: You don't have her name yet, not quite—it's sitting right at the back of your teeth like a word you almost remember from another life. What you do know is that she isn't a stray customer, and she's been watching you from the very beginning.
teases.text: The dream of gold lanterns and a laughing woman has lingered all week. When {alias} slips into your office, {form}, and you catch the scent of cedar smoke and warm wax, you know immediately where you've smelled it before. "Oh, you will pay for that look," she promises, taking hold of your collar.

choices.label: "You brought me here."
choices.res: "I brought you somewhere interesting," she corrects softly, leaving you breathless against your own desk before vanishing into the hall.
choices.resIn: She doesn't deny it. Instead, she backs you against the edge of your desk with a slow, wicked grin. "Clever boy. Now let's see if you're good with your hands too."

choices.label: Reach for the name on your tongue
choices.res: The syllables slip away before you can catch them, and {alias} laughs softly, pressing two warm fingers over your lips. "Almost, {sam}. Next time."

teases.title: Different Ears, Same Girl

image.comp: a woman in a disguise walking around a man's chair, trailing a hand across his shoulders, playful teasing smile

teases.intro:
{alias} has new ears today, {form}, and the exact same everything else. She walks around your chair in a slow, unhurried circle, trailing a warm hand across your shoulders.

"What do you think? Do I suit it?" she asks, leaning down until her cheek nearly brushes yours.
teases.wonder: You know you're onto her, and you know you're still missing one crucial piece—a name sitting right on the edge of memory.
teases.text: {alias} has new ears today, {form}, and the same everything else. She walks around you in a slow circle, trailing a hand across your shoulders. "What do you think? Do I suit it?"

choices.label: Call after her as she slips away
choices.res: "Whoever you are..." Your voice carries down the empty hall, answered only by a faint, delighted laugh.

choices.label: Catch her wrist before she vanishes
choices.res: "Quick reflexes," {alias} purrs, rewarding you with a slow, dizzying distraction before slipping through your fingers like smoke.
choices.resIn: Your fingers close around her warm wrist, and {alias} raises both eyebrows in pleasant surprise before stepping straight into your arms.

teases.title: Say My Name

image.comp: a woman straddling a man's lap with arms around his neck, forehead against his, startled delighted smile, candles flaring gold around them
image.setting: bedroom at night, every candle burning bright gold

teases.intro:
She comes to you as {alias} tonight, {form}, wearing a smile that is just a little too wide. She settles onto your lap in the armchair, loops both arms around your neck, and leans in—and you let her. You let her come all the way to the edge of a kiss.

Then, quietly, you say, "{goddess}."

Everything stops. Her smile stays where it is; her eyes don't. Every candle in the room dips and flares gold at once. You don't know where the name came from—a dream of paper lanterns, a woman swinging her heels in the dark, an old promise about a debt. It was simply there on your tongue.

"...Well," she says, in a voice that isn't {alias}'s anymore—deeper, warmer, and ringing slightly like struck brass. "That took you long enough."
teases.wonder: The disguise hasn't vanished, not quite, but the woman sitting in your lap is suddenly unmistakable: the Lamplighter herself, warm and solid and looking at you like you just won a bet she didn't expect to lose.
teases.text: She settles onto your lap as {alias}, {form}, and leans in to kiss you. Right before her lips touch yours, you say, "{goddess}." Every candle in the room flares gold. "...Well," she says, in a voice that isn't {alias}'s anymore. "That took you long enough."

choices.label: "You've been teasing me for cycles."
choices.res: "And you kept falling for it," Seliora purrs, kissing you breathless before slipping out of your lap like smoke. "Now the real game starts, {sam}."
choices.resIn: "Guilty," Seliora murmurs, her amber eyes glowing in the candlelight as her hands slide down your chest. "And since you finally earned my name, I suppose you deserve a proper reward."

choices.label: "So what happens now?"
choices.res: Seliora rests her forehead against yours, smiling softly. "Now I stop pretending I'm just passing through, {sam}—and you see how far you can push your luck."

teases.title: House Rules

image.comp: a poised woman in round spectacles and a scholar's coat standing in an office doorway with hands on her hips, playful grin
image.setting: dim study at night, warm lantern light on a desk

teases.intro:
The knock on the door is very polite. You have been waiting for it, in a way; there was a note on your desk this morning in handwriting you didn't recognize, saying only: "Lessons, seven o'clock."

When the door swings open, {alias}, {form}, stands in the threshold with her hands on her hips, round spectacles perched on her nose, and amber eyes bright with mischief. "Mr. {sam}? I'm here about the private lesson. I understand it's... hands-on."
teases.wonder: You know who she is. She knows you know, and both of you are going to pretend very seriously that neither of you does—just to see who cracks first.
teases.text: Seliora arrives at your office dressed as {form}, spectacles perched on her nose. "Mr. {sam}? I'm here about the private lesson. I understand it's... hands-on."

choices.label: Play along with a straight face
choices.res: Neither of you keeps a straight face for more than two minutes, and she leaves you dizzy, breathless, and laughing against your desk.
choices.resIn: "A retake? Already?" She sets down the book, eyes dancing. "Very well. Let's see what you remember."

choices.label: Beg for extra credit
choices.res: "Begging. Good start." She glows with satisfaction—and leaves you high and dry without awarding a single point.
choices.resIn: "Extra credit?" She taps her chin as if it's a serious question. "That depends. How badly do you want it?"

teases.title: Introductions

image.comp: a woman in a disguise standing inside an office doorway with one hand inside his coat, glowing amber eyes, wickedly innocent smile
image.setting: office at night, warm desk lantern

teases.intro:
{alias}, {form}, knocks on the office door and waits to be asked in—an act of restraint that is not at all like her.

"Good evening. I'm new in town." She holds out a hand, perfectly innocent. "I heard the owner could use some help." Her eyes are glowing gold, and her free hand is already sliding inside your coat.

"You haven't introduced yourself," you say, and she gives you a look that says play along or suffer.
teases.wonder: She is terrible at pretending to be a shy applicant, and clearly having the time of her life.
teases.text: {alias}, {form}, knocks politely on your office door with glowing amber eyes and a hand already inside your coat. "Good evening. I'm new in town. I heard the owner could use some help."

choices.label: "Welcome. What can you do?"
choices.res: "Oh," says the stranger, "a great many things." She shows you several of them—none to completion. You are going to be walking funny for a while.
choices.resIn: "Oh," says the stranger, brightening, "a great many things." She closes the office door with her heel and does not look at all innocent.

choices.label: "{goddess}, you're a terrible actor."
choices.res: "Rude," Seliora says, pinching your ribs before laughing softly. "Fine, no audition. Come have tea with me before I decide to make you miserable."

teases.title: A New Face, an Old Game

image.comp: a woman lounging across a wooden office desk, bare foot sliding up his thigh, teasing smirk

teases.intro:
Tonight she's {alias}, {form}, lounging across your desk and pretending very hard that you haven't met.

"I'm sure I'd remember a man like you," she says smoothly, as her bare foot slides slowly up the inside of your thigh under the desk.
teases.wonder:
You play along, because it's easier than arguing and because you're curious how long she can hold the straight face. Not long, from the look of it: the corner of her mouth keeps betraying her.

You wonder whether tonight is the night she'll let you finish. You doubt it—her toes are very warm and entirely too confident.
teases.text: Tonight she's {alias}, {form}, lounging across your desk as her foot slides up the inside of your thigh. "I'm sure I'd remember a man like you," she purrs.

choices.label: Play along with her
choices.res: She is very good, and absolutely merciless, leaving you exactly one breath from the edge before slipping out into the hall.
choices.resIn: You catch her ankle and hold her gaze. {alias} laughs softly, sliding off the desk straight into your lap.

choices.label: Give her the satisfaction of her name
choices.res: "Seliora," you say evenly. She beams like she just won a prize, kisses your temple, and vanishes.

teases.title: Pick a Name

image.comp: a striking woman leaning against an upstairs hallway wall under a lantern, confident teasing smile
image.setting: upstairs corridor at night, warm brass wall lantern

teases.intro:
{alias}, {form}, is waiting in the upstairs hall, leaning against the wall under a brass lantern as though she owned the house—which, strictly speaking, she might.

"Have we done business before?" she asks smoothly as you come up the stairs, tilting her head so the lantern light catches the gold threads in her dark hair.
teases.wonder:
You play along, because it's easier than arguing and because you're curious how long she can hold the straight face. Not long, from the look of it: the corner of her mouth keeps betraying her.

You wonder whether tonight is the night she'll let you finish. You doubt it—the look in her eyes says she already has a plan.
teases.text: {alias}, {form}, leans under the upstairs lantern with an innocent smile. "Have we done business before?"

choices.label: Stay in character
choices.res: She leaves laughing, a little breathless and thoroughly pleased with herself, while you lean against the banister catching your breath.
choices.resIn: You pretend to think hard, and she pretends to be impatient, until she grabs your tie and pulls you into the nearest empty room.

choices.label: Call her Seliora
choices.res: "A point," she says, thrilled, and rewards you with a slow, pointed kiss right under the lantern before vanishing down the hall.

teases.title: No Disguise

image.comp: a luminous goddess with long black hair threaded with gold and glowing amber eyes standing close beside a moonlit window, soft sincere smile
image.setting: bedroom at night, pale moonlight and warm gold glow

teases.intro:
There is no borrowed cloak tonight, no spectacles, no merchant jacket. When you turn around from the window, she is standing in the center of your room in {form}—luminous skin, night-black hair threaded with living gold, and eyes burning like steady lantern flames.

For once, she doesn't have a quip ready. She simply looks at you, waiting to see if you'll step back now that the mortal mask is off.
teases.wonder: She looks breathtaking, and a little bit uncertain—which somehow makes her feel closer than she ever did in disguise.
teases.text: She appears in your room in {form}—no borrowed face, just night-black hair threaded with gold and eyes like lantern flame—watching quietly to see how you react.

choices.label: Step close and kiss her
choices.res: She melts into your arms with a soft, startled sigh, kissing you back with dizzying heat before reluctantly pulling away at the threshold.
choices.resIn: You close the distance without hesitating and kiss her slowly. Seliora lets out a quiet, breathless sound against your lips, her hands tangling in your hair as the golden light around her softens to a warm glow.

choices.label: "You don't need the disguises."
choices.res: A genuine flush rises across her luminous cheeks. "Flatterer," she murmurs, resting her hand briefly over your heart. "Keep saying things like that, {sam}, and I might stay like this."

teases.title: What It Costs

image.comp: a goddess in midnight and gold silk sitting on the edge of a bed, holding his hands, serious warm amber eyes

teases.intro:
Seliora sits on the edge of your bed in {form}, turning one of your hands over in hers and tracing the lines across your palm with a thumb that feels almost humanly warm.

"You keep asking why I always stop before the end," she says quietly, looking up through her lashes. "It isn't cruelty, {sam}. A god who gives herself completely to a mortal—skin, breath, release—ties her spark to that body. If you finish inside me, the tether locks. No more slipping between worlds. Just one life, one house, and whatever years we get."
teases.wonder: She isn't teasing at all tonight. She is laying the entire price on the table so you can't claim you didn't know.
teases.text: Seated on the edge of your bed in {form}, Seliora traces your palm and explains quietly why she always pulls back at the brink: finishing inside her will lock her divine spark into a single mortal life.

choices.label: "Then I'll wait until you're ready."
choices.res: Seliora looks at you for a long, quiet moment, her amber eyes softening. "Careful, {sam}," she whispers, kissing your cheek. "You're making it very hard not to be ready."

choices.label: "That doesn't scare me."
choices.res: "Good," she breathes, dark eyes gleaming as she pushes you back onto the quilts. "Because I'm still going to make you work for it."
choices.resIn: Seliora smiles—a slow, fierce, entirely womanly smile—and leans in to kiss your throat. "Then let's see how much patience you really have."

teases.title: Razor's Edge

image.comp: a luminous goddess straddling a man's lap on rumpled sheets, flushed and breathless, forehead pressed against his
image.setting: bedroom at night, warm golden candlelight

teases.intro:
She straddles your lap on the mattress in {form}, sheer midnight silk slipping off her shoulders, breathing hard as her hips roll slowly against yours. Every time you reach for her waist to pull her down, she catches your wrists—trembling slightly herself.

"Not yet," Seliora breathes against your lips, sounding half-convinced and completely undone. "Almost, {sam}. Almost."
teases.wonder: Her composure is hanging by a thread. Another cycle or two, and she won't be the one pulling back.
teases.text: Straddling your lap in {form}, flushed and breathless, Seliora catches your wrists as your hips lift to meet hers. "Almost, {sam}," she whispers against your mouth. "Almost."

choices.label: Hold her close and match her breath
choices.res: She shudders in your arms, pressing hot kisses along your jaw before slipping away at the very last heartbeat with a ragged, breathless laugh.
choices.resIn: You let her set the pace, your hands warm on her bare back as she grinds against you with parted lips and half-closed eyes.

teases.title: What Do You Want?

image.comp: a goddess in midnight and gold silk leaning against a moonlit balcony railing, glancing back over her shoulder with a soft fond smile
image.setting: lantern-lit balcony overlooking Hollowmere at night

teases.intro:
You find Seliora out on the upper balcony in {form}, leaning on the stone rail as she watches the streetlamps flicker to life down the avenue.

"Tell me honestly, {sam}," she says without turning around, though you can hear the smile in her voice. "When I finally let you tie me down to mud and bone—what are you going to do with me?"
teases.wonder: Under the golden glow of the streetlamps, she doesn't look like an untouchable deity at all—just a woman waiting to hear what she means to you.
teases.text: Standing on the balcony in {form}, Seliora watches the streetlamps below and asks softly, "When I finally let you tie me down to mud and bone—what are you going to do with me?"

choices.label: "Keep you warm, fed, and thoroughly spoiled."
choices.res: Seliora laughs—bright and unguarded—and pulls you back through the balcony doors. "Acceptable terms, {sam}."
choices.resIn: She turns around with glowing amber eyes and loops her arms around your neck. "Promises, promises. Start right now."

choices.label: "Put you to work on the ledgers."
choices.res: She stares at you in deadpan silence for three seconds, then bursts out laughing. "Careful, mortal—I might actually take you up on that."
